correctness.rationale: For every lambda>0, M and A are (S∓|D|)/2. The symmetric Skellam pmf plus k I_k(z)=z(I_{k-1}-I_{k+1})/2 telescopes to d(lambda)=E|D|=2 lambda q_lambda. Differentiating the joint Poisson series gives Cov(S,f(D))=lambda d/dlambda E f(D); applying this to |D| and the Bessel derivative identities yields d'=2 r_lambda. Together with Var(S)=2 lambda and E D^2=2 lambda this gives the exact variances. Standard fixed-order Bessel asymptotics then give the stated Fano expansions. The checker independently reproduces the formulas from truncated joint sums; finite checks are not used as proof.

value.rationale: Poisson order statistics are used for replicated count extrema, and prior work highlights their underdispersion without quantifying its size. The two-sample case is the first nontrivial order-statistic setting; exact finite-intensity moments and the universal 1-1/pi dispersion limit identify the magnitude of the variance reduction and reveal an asymmetric approach of min and max that qualitative ultra-log-concavity cannot see. This is a natural structural refinement, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
